paper.title: Function-Correcting Codes With Data Protection
paper.tldr: This work proposes a general framework that offers protection for both the data and the function values inFunction-correcting codes and presents explicit constructions of FCCs with data protection for specific families of functions, such as locally bounded functions and the Hamming weight function.

paper.title: Coding Theory: A First Course
paper.tldr: This book gives a comprehensive introduction to coding theory whilst only assuming basic linear algebra and contains a detailed and rigorous introduction to the theory of block codes and moves on to more advanced topics like BCH codes, Goppa codes and Sudan's algorithm for list decoding.

paper.title: Unequal Error Protection: An Information-Theoretic Perspective
paper.tldr: It is shown that, feedback results in a significant improvement in both bit-wise and message-wise UEPs (except the single message case for missed detection).

paper.title: Function-Correcting Codes
paper.tldr: This work shows that function-correcting codes are equivalent to irregular distance codes, i.e., codes that obey some given distance requirement between each pair of codewords, and derives general upper and lower bounds on their optimal redundancy.

paper.title: Surface code quantum computing by lattice surgery
paper.tldr: This paper introduces a new technique enabling the coupling of two planar codes without transversal operations, maintaining the 2DNN of the encoded computer, and shows how lattice surgery allows us to distribute encoded GHZ states in a more direct manner, and how a demonstration of an encoded CNOT between two distance-3 logical states is possible with 53 physical qubits.

paper.title: Fusion-based quantum computation
paper.tldr: A quantum computation scheme where the same measurements used to generate entanglement can also be used to achieve fault-tolerance leading to an increased tolerance to errors leading to a model for fault tolerant quantum computing constructed from physical primitives readily accessible in photonic systems.
